teams.heading: Fiji drop to bottom of Nations Championship log after Scotland defeat
teams.body: Fiji go into the weekend bottom of the Nations Championship log after a 17-33 loss against Scotland in Round 3. The Flying Fijians have failed to secure a victory in their opening three tournament matches. They have conceded 145 points in those three games, while scoring 49 points in the same three-match window. Attention now turns to their next fixture against France, who defeated Fiji 34-21 in November 2025.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs accuses RFU of having 'blinkers on' over Steve Borthwick's contract
teams.body: Former England scrum-half Ben Youngs has criticised the RFU for extending Steve Borthwick's contract, claiming performance director Conor O'Shea has "some blinkers on." The RFU handed Borthwick an extension through to the end of the 2028 Six Nations, despite a 2026 campaign featuring five Test defeats, including a first-ever loss to Italy. Speaking on the *For The Love Of Rugby* podcast, Youngs questioned the timing of the decision ahead of next year's World Cup, warning that union bosses remain accountable if the campaign fails.

teams.heading: Tommy O’Brien targets 2027 World Cup after injury-enforced Nations Championship absence
teams.body: Leinster back Tommy O’Brien has set his sights on the 2027 World Cup after a groin injury forced him to miss Ireland’s recent Nations Championship tour. O’Brien, who earned nine caps during a breakthrough season featuring tries against England and Scotland, was sidelined after sustaining the injury during the United Rugby Championship final at Croke Park. Despite the setback, the 28-year-old remains determined to reach his peak for the tournament in Australia, describing the prospect as the "pinnacle of my career" following his 11th-hour omission from the squad.

teams.heading: Ben Carter cleared for season start following Nations Championship ankle injury
teams.body: Ben Carter is fit for the United Rugby Championship season after recovering from the ankle injury that curtailed his Nations Championship campaign. The Dragons lock, who started six consecutive Tests for Wales before being sidelined in July, has avoided surgery and is expected to feature in his club’s opener on 25 September. Defence coach Dale MacLeod confirmed Carter is in the "best nick" he has seen, providing Steve Tandy with a key reinforcement ahead of the November meeting with Japan.

lead.why: It confirms the return to fitness of a regular Wales starter who had been sidelined since the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Argentina reflects on series draw as focus turns to Ireland challenge
teams.body: Following the hard-fought 28-28 draw in Mendoza last weekend, Argentina’s two-match series against Australia has officially concluded. With the series now behind them, the squad’s attention shifts to their upcoming Round 4 fixture against Ireland. Coach Felipe Contepomi will look to build on the grit displayed in the series finale as the team prepares for the next phase of the international calendar.

teams.heading: James Slipper pauses playing career to join the Brumbies coaching staff
teams.body: Wallabies centurion James Slipper has been appointed as the Brumbies' new scrum coach on a temporary basis. The 154-Test veteran, who recently signed a one-year contract extension, will step away from on-field duties during the upcoming Super Rugby AUS campaign to focus on his new role. Slipper, the most capped prop in international history, aims to mentor the next generation of forwards while maintaining his status as an emergency option for the Wallabies' 2027 World Cup squad.

teams.heading: Richie Mo'unga returns as Dave Rennie reshuffles for Baltimore Test finale
teams.body: Richie Mo'unga will make his first Test appearance since the 2023 World Cup final after being named to start at fly-half against the Springboks in Baltimore. Following tour-ending injuries to Ardie Savea, Luke Jacobson and Quinn Tupaea, head coach Dave Rennie has confirmed Codie Taylor will captain the side. Rennie noted that the changes were planned, stating: “Every player here has worked incredibly hard over the last seven weeks to prepare the team for the seven games we’ve played so far.”

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus reaches 100 Tests in charge of the Springboks
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus will oversee his 100th Test as Springbok boss in this weekend’s series finale in Baltimore. Erasmus has served as head coach for 60 Tests across two spells, having previously guided the team as director of rugby during Jacques Nienaber’s 39-Test tenure. Since 2018, the Springboks have maintained a 73.7% win rate under his oversight, securing back-to-back World Cup titles and three Rugby Championship trophies, and he now seeks to celebrate this century with a series victory.

lead.why: The milestone of a head coach reaching 100 Tests overseeing the Springboks is a significant narrative for this weekend's series finale.
